issue_title: fix: Data loss in normalize_whitespace silently converts non-string values to NaN in mixed object columns
issue_body:
### What happened?

When calling `ar.normalize_whitespace` on an `object` column containing mixed types (e.g. a mix of strings, integers, and booleans—which is extremely common in raw, uncleaned CSV inputs), the function calls the pandas `.str` accessor (`df[col].str.replace().str.strip()`). 

The `.str` accessor silently converts all non-string elements (like numbers or booleans) to `NaN`. This leads to silent, permanent data loss of all non-string values inside the targeted columns without raising any warnings or exceptions.

### Area

C++ cleaning engine

### Minimal reproduction

import arnio as ar
import pandas as pd

# Create a mixed-type object column
df = pd.DataFrame({"col": ["hello  world", 42, True]})
frame = ar.from_pandas(df)

# Run normalize_whitespace on the mixed column
clean_frame = ar.normalize_whitespace(frame, columns=["col"])

# Display result
print(ar.to_pandas(clean_frame)["col"].tolist())
# Output: ['hello world', <NA>, <NA>]
# Note that 42 and True were permanently deleted and replaced by NaN/null

### Expected behavior

The function should dynamically check the type of each element or cast only string-like values, preserving numeric and boolean values in mixed-type columns.

### Actual behavior

All non-string elements in the processed object columns are silently destroyed and replaced by NaN / null values.

### Impact

Blocks installation or import

### Arnio version

1.1.0

### Install method

pip install arnio

### Operating System

macOS

### Python version

3.12.4

### Environment details

```shell
Pandas 2.x, NumPy 1.2x, Python 3.12.4
```

### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I searched existing issues and did not find a duplicate.
- [x] I included a minimal reproduction or explained why one is not possible.

### Additional context

This issue affects data quality pipelines where data cleaning is performed on raw, uncoerced inputs containing mixed types.
pr_title: fix: fixed Data loss in normalize_whitespace
pr_body: ## Summary `normalize_whitespace` called the pandas `.str` accessor directly on `object`-dtype columns. Pandas `.str` silently coerces non-string elements (integers, booleans, floats) to `NaN`, causing permanent silent data loss on mixed-type columns — common in raw, uncleaned CSV input. Fix replaces the `.str.replace().str.strip()` chain with an element-wise `.map()` call that applies whitespace normalization only to `str` instances and passes all other values through untouched. ## Linked issue Fixes #1927 ## Type of change - [x] Bug fix - [ ] Feature - [ ] Performance improvement - [ ] Documentation - [x] Tests - [ ] Refactor - [ ] CI / packaging ## Area - [ ] CSV parser / I/O - [x] C++ cleaning engine - [x] Python API / ArFrame - [ ] Pipeline / custom steps - [ ] Data quality / profiling - [ ] Schema validation - [x] pandas interoperability - [ ] Docs / website - [ ] Developer tooling ## Testing ```bash pytest tests/test_normalize_whitespace.py -v # 27 passed in 0.63s ``` All 27 tests pass, including 3 new regression tests added for this fix. - [x] `make test` (or `python -m pytest tests -v --cov=arnio`) - [ ] `make lint` - [ ] optionally `python -m pytest tests -v --tb=short -x` - [ ] Other: ## Screenshots / Media Before (bug): ```python >>> df = pd.DataFrame({"col": ["hello world", 42, True]}) >>> ar.to_pandas(ar.normalize_whitespace(ar.from_pandas(df), columns=["col"]))["col"].tolist() ['hello world', , ] # 42 and True silently destroyed ``` After (fix): ```python >>> ar.to_pandas(ar.normalize_whitespace(ar.from_pandas(df), columns=["col"]))["col"].tolist() ['hello world', '42', 'True'] # no data loss ``` ## Performance Impact No measurable impact on purely string columns. Mixed-type `object` columns now use `.map()` instead of `.str`, which is slightly slower but these columns were previously producing incorrect results — correctness takes priority. ## GSSoC labels ## Contributor checklist - [x] I read the contributing guide. - [x] I kept the PR focused on one issue or one logical change. - [x] I added or updated tests for behavior changes. - [ ] I added or updated docs/examples for public API changes. - [x] I checked that generated files, logs, and local build artifacts are not committed. - [x] My PR title uses Conventional Commits (`fix: preserve non-string values in normalize_whitespace for mixed-type object columns`) ## Maintainer notes The fix is intentionally minimal — one function, one loop, no changes to validation logic or the pipeline registration. `isinstance(val, str)` is used over `pd.api.types.is_string_dtype` because the latter checks column-level dtype and returns `True` for all `object` columns regardless of element types.
